title: Conviction and Deterrence of Road Touts
what_it_is: Conviction and Deterrence of Road Touts

sections.label: Road touting convictions data
sections.summary: This data was given in the reply to Member Melvin Yong's question last month, and there was no conviction for road touting in the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This data was given in the reply to Member Melvin Yong’s question last month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: There was no conviction for road touting in the last five years.

sections.label: Handling road touting offences
sections.summary: The public, especially motorists, know how to handle road touts, and authorities will look at facts and take action where necessary.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Our sense is that members of the public, especially the motorists, know how to handle road touts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In essence, while there are Police reports being made, there are those who also seek guidance and help from their insurers as well as legal counsel for civil remedies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: If you look at road touts, we will look at the case where there may be other offences that have been committed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, road touting itself is an offence and so, we will look at the Miscellaneous Offences (Public Order and Nuisance) Act.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Within it, depending on the facts and the circumstances of the case, they may be involved in some road traffic offences, Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) offences and so forth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Essentially, we will look at the facts of the case and at the same time, it is clear that touting in any form is an offence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: If at any point in time there are reports and we see this as a serious matter, we will take action where necessary.
